claims.text: A machine-learning potential can accelerate TOR-TILD calculations for multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Machine-learning-potential acceleration produces faster molecular-dynamics simulations.
Accelerated molecular dynamics reduces computational cost.
Reduced computational cost permits more extensive sampling of configuration space.
More extensive configuration-space sampling improves the accuracy of solid-to-fluid transition calculations.
The accelerated method will improve determination of the transition temperature relative to existing computational and experimental baselines.
The accelerated method will improve determination of fusion enthalpy relative to existing computational and experimental baselines.
The accelerated method will improve determination of fusion entropy relative to existing computational and experimental baselines.
The accelerated method will improve determination of the volume change at the transition relative to existing computational and experimental baselines.
The accelerated method will improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity relative to existing computational and experimental baselines.
The accelerated method will be more computationally efficient than TOR-TILD without acceleration.
The approach is applicable only within systems and temperature ranges for which the machine-learning potential has been trained and validated.
Transfer of the machine-learning potential to unseen compositions is uncertain.
The machine-learning potential may introduce bias into accelerated simulations.
Significant deviations beyond expected uncertainty from direct TOR-TILD or experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
